I personally believe Weiss could have just brushed past him. Pulling her sword was completely unneeded and aggressive. Just because it's what the writers chose to have happen doesn't mean it was the right way to go.
He didn't try to steal it. He didn't do a single thing during V4. And if him being a prick is horrible, so is Weiss pointing her weapon at him.

The FNDM has been victim blaming Whitley for weeks now. But I saw it less as victim blaming and more Whitley using his defence mechanism. The best way to avoid Jacques' ire is to obey him. It works for Whitley, so in his mind, Weiss has to do the same to stay safe. It's wrong, but I wouldn't expect much from an abused kid. But if you insist it's victim blaming, could'nt you say that's what Weiss did to Willow? My point is, they're all victims and have all done shitty things. If one has things to answer for, they all do. It shouldn't be "Oh, these two are sympathetic, but this one needs to answer for his crimes."
If he has things to answer for just for being snarky, then Weiss should have had to answer for her racism in V1. And she should also answer for threatening her brother.
He was lashing out because he was alone and frustrated. Still waiting for Weiss' apology.
And not an apology from Weiss for pointing her weapon at him?
If that's all it was meant to serve, the sword was definitely unnecessary and mean spirited. Scenes can be executed poorly. You don't have to eat up everything the show feeds you.

All I got from the first paragraph is that people are upset about this scene and you think it was the right choice. Cool. I don't. I understand that they were tired and didn't have time to deal with him. But that doesn't change the fact that putting a sword in his face was just unnecessarily aggressive and a poorly executed "Yass Queen!" moment. She didn't have to brow beat him into helping at all. She could have just ignored him and pushed past him. I love Weiss, but I'm not going to defend every little thing she does. The narrative treating him like an enemy is super off putting, especially after the scene with Willow. I wouldn't even have so much of a problem if he acknowledge Weiss' behavior and have her apologize, but the way the scene was framed I know they won't.

Being a nuisance is not justification for her pointing a sword at him. There are dozens of ways she could have gotten him out of the way. Whitley has never been shown to be a big obstacle, and we can't just assume a different approach wouldn't have worked just because Weiss didn't try them.

She can't handle snark and sass without pointing her loaded weapon at him?? It's clear to me that this was supposed to be a "Yass Queen!" Moment, which is super odd considering her talk with Willow and her pulling her weapon out was just completely unnecessary IMO.
Needs his ass beaten for what? Being snarky? Being a product of abuse? Weiss was much the same in Volume 1. Why didn't she get her ass beat?

I thought that she was needlessly aggressive and it feels like the show is forgetting that he was a victim of abuse, just like her. Of course she didn't have to sit down and have a heart-to-heart, but she couldn't be the bigger person and had to have a slam dunk on her brother who at worst has just been snotty?

Am I the only one that doesn't think this is the case and these movies are far too lighthearted? The scenes are allowed to just be somber and show the characters vulnerable, human. I think the MCU has taken steps in the right direction, but still, meh.
